subject: Helix Health - Orderflow: MSA clause removal, capacity delta & change order
messages:
From: Sariah Bloom <sariah.bloom@helixhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@helixhealth.com
Date: 2027-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helix Health - Orderflow: MSA clause removal, capacity delta & change order

Markus —

Thanks for the heads up on timing. Our legal team pushed one more set of notes this morning (attached) that requests removal of Section 7.4 (audits) and asks for clearer language around the throughput uplift trigger. They're also asking for an explicit formula for prorated credits if we top up mid-quarter. Can you confirm whether Redwood is comfortable removing 7.4 entirely, or if we need to translate it into a lower-impact observability clause?

Separately, procurement asked for a third-party attestation on the billing math — I've included our finance lead on cc. If you can reply with an action plan and an estimated turnaround for a signed change order, we can queue the internal approval.

Thanks,
Sariah
Senior Contracts Manager
Helix Health

Attachments: helix_legal_notes_v2.docx (docx)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sariah Bloom <sariah.bloom@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helix Health - Orderflow: MSA clause removal, capacity delta & change order

Sariah —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Internal summary below and next steps attached (helix_redline_v3). TL;DR: we can remove the auditing clause as written but request a limited replacement that preserves log retention and notice obligations (proposed language in redline). For the throughput uplift/proration, we've drafted a formula in the workbook (capacity_topup_calc.xlsx) that shows how credits/prorate are applied by daily effective date.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll send a clean change order with tracked redlines by end of day tomorrow (3/30).
- If Helix legal accepts the limited-observability replacement, we can sign the CO and execute via DocuSign the same week.
- Karthik and Laura — looping you both for legal/finance sign-off on the wording and proration math. Please flag any must-have constraints.

Questions for Helix: do you need an attestation letter for the billing calc (one-off) or ongoing statement of accuracy? We can provide a one-time finance reconciliation PDF signed by our revenue ops.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix_redline_v3.docx (redline), capacity_topup_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-29T13:37:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Helix Health - Orderflow: MSA clause removal, capacity delta & change order

Karthik / Laura —

Forwarding Sariah's note and our proposed redline. Key asks summarized so we can be crisp with legal and finance: 

1) Section 7.4 (audits) — Helix wants removal. We should accept removal but add short replacement language: "retention and notice for forensic requests up to 90 days; no live intrusion." See helix_redline_v3, p.3. Karthik: is that adequate from a risk perspective?

2) Throughput uplift proration — Helix needs a deterministic formula for mid-quarter top-ups. I populated the calc tab and an example scenario for 3/15 top-up. Laura: can Revenue Ops sign off on the exported calc and provide a one-time attestation PDF? If not, what minimal evidence would satisfy procurement?

3) Signature path & timeline — They want the CO this week. If we can get legal/finance sign-off by EOD 3/30, I'll route DocuSign for exec signature.

Please reply with any redlines or 'stop' items. If neither of you have objections, I'll proceed with the clean CO.

Date: 2027-03-30T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Helix change order and signature path (DocuSign link)

Sariah —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal review, Redwood is comfortable removing Section 7.4 and replacing it with the two-paragraph observability substitute noted in helix_redline_v3. I've attached a clean change order plus the signed one-time attestation template that Laura's team will use (attestation_financial.pdf — attached to DocuSign envelope).

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/hellink/HLX-042-changeorder

Requested approvals and items for Helix to confirm before signing:
- Confirm replacement language in Section 2.1 of the CO is acceptable (short text reproduced below).
- Confirm acceptance of the proration formula in the workbook for mid-quarter top-ups.
- Indicate whether you need the attestation as a standalone PDF prior to signing or if it can be included in the executed CO envelope.

If we get a green light by EOD Thursday (3/31), we can have signatures completed and the capacity uplift scheduled for the first run window in April.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

-----BEGIN QUOTE-----
Replacement language (excerpt): "Customer and Redwood agree to replace Section 7.4 with limited-forensic access language. Redwood will retain necessary request logs for a minimum of 90 days and will provide Customer with written notice prior to any forensic access. Redwood will not permit live interactive access to production systems for audit purposes absent court order or regulatory requirement."
-----END QUOTE-----

Attachments in envelope: change_order_HLX-042_clean.pdf, helix_redline_v3.docx, capacity_topup_calc.xlsx, attestation_financial_template.pdf
